text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- European summit urges all parties to support Mubarak's efforts aimed at saving the peace process. European Union leaders call on Israel to recognise the right of Palestinians to determine their own fate.
- President reviews plan to renovate al-Azhar mosque. Mubarak urges speedy renovation of the mosque and its surrounding areas.
- Defence Minister Tantawi holds military talks in Greece.
- African support for Mubarak's efforts towards peace and development; President discussed with OAU secretary general Salem results of OAU summit in Harare.
- Mubarak meets African information ministers and affirms Egypt's support for African issues.
- Foreign Minister Moussa says in Italy after talks with officials there that Middle East peace process is not dead and that Egypt and Europe are working to save it.
- Washington praises Mubarak's efforts to save peace process.
- Public Enterprise Minister Atef Obeid says government has sold five companies to Egyptian investors for total of 1.2 billion pounds.
- Mubarak's gift to Egypt's youth -- 20,000 flats at reduced price.
- Mubarak and Chirac to discuss in Paris today crisis in peace talks, results of European summit and economic cooperation.
- Capital Markets Authority wants to impose insurance policy on brokerage firms to ensure they fuflil obligations to investors.
- Prosecution asks for life sentence for the spy Azam and his accomplices.
- Six years in prison for Briton who stole Egyptian antiquities.
